title: Introducing CSS Grid 🕸️
description: Understand the two‑dimensional layout system, the container‑item relationship, and grid terminology.

slides.title: Grid: The Ultimate Layout Engine 🏗️
slides.content:
# Two‑Dimensional Control

While Flexbox excels at one‑dimensional layouts (row **or** column), CSS Grid is built for **rows and columns simultaneously**. You define a grid structure on a parent container and place children into cells, areas, or spanning tracks.

Grid lets you create complex page layouts with fewer hacks, precise control over alignment, and overlapping elements. It's been supported in all modern browsers since 2017.

slides.title: Grid Container and Grid Items 🧱
slides.content:
# Just Like Flexbox, But Richer - **Grid container** – the element with `display: grid;` (or `inline-grid`). - **Grid items** – direct children of the container. Only direct children participate in the grid. ```html
A
B
C
``` As with Flexbox, grandchildren are not grid items unless their own parent is also a grid container.

quizData.question: Setting `display: grid;` on a parent makes all its descendants grid items.
quizData.explanation: Only direct children become grid items. Nested elements need their own grid container to participate.

slides.title: Key Grid Terminology 📚
slides.content:
# Tracks, Lines, Cells, Areas

- **Grid tracks** – rows or columns (the spaces between grid lines).
- **Grid lines** – the horizontal and vertical dividing lines that form the grid. They are numbered starting from 1 (or -1 for the opposite end).
- **Grid cell** – the smallest single unit, like a spreadsheet cell.
- **Grid area** – any rectangle of adjacent cells (an item can span multiple columns and rows).

Think of the grid as a sheet of graph paper: lines are the gridlines, cells are the squares, and an area is a group of squares merged together.

quizData.question: If you only define `grid-template-columns: 100px 200px;` and have six items, how many columns will the grid have?
quizData.explanation: The grid has two explicit columns; extra items wrap into new rows automatically.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use Firefox DevTools for Grid

Firefox's inspector has a fantastic grid visualiser that shows line numbers, track sizes, and area names. It's a game‑changer for learning and debugging.
